result.title: What Makes a Good Move? Learning to Act from Experience in Visual Worlds
result.summary: Learning visual policies requires turning interaction experience into guidance for individual decisions. Trajectory outcomes obscure action quality, while unguided exploration can revisit familiar situations. We present \textsc{LightAct}, an experience-learning framework that connects skill-guided exploration with policy internalization. Interaction segments are summarized into experience entries and consolidated into a game-specific skill that guides root collection toward broader state coverage. At each root, candidate actions are compared through short rollouts under a shared frozen policy. Environment-reported score gains are averaged across continuations and normalized into relative action rewards, producing reusable supervision for reinforcement learning. Policy training uses a compact dataset of just 1,024 decision roots collected in a single source game and paired with their action rewards. Across 170 GameWorld tasks spanning 34 games, \textsc{LightAct} improves overall progress by 23.6, 29.2, and 13.0 percentage points at the 2B, 4B, and 9B scales, respectively, with our strongest model competitive with reported proprietary-model results. Ablations show broader root-state coverage with skill guidance and consistent gains across three policy optimizers. Case studies show how rollouts distinguish actions with identical immediate gains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LightAct 框架：把交互片段总结为经验条目并固化为游戏技能以引导探索，在每个决策根上用共享冻结策略的短 rollout 比较候选动作，将环境分数增益归一化为相对动作奖励，用于强化学习训练，并在 170 个 GameWorld 任务上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用短 rollout 区分「即时增益相同」的动作并构造监督信号，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、贡献分配与停止决策提供可核查的线索；但论文本身研究游戏视觉策略而非 latent 推理状态。
